name: Gunrunner
overview: A major traverse connecting all four Gunsight peaks (Northeast, North, Middle, South), offering sustained alpine crack climbing on excellent granite with breathtaking remote alpine positioning.
beta: Traverse all four major summits on north-facing ascents and south-facing descents. Features 18 pitches of mostly new climbing: three pitches of 5.10 crack climbing with one aid point used to escape a dead-end fist crack near North Peak summit. Rappel descent includes free-hanging rappel over moat onto Blue Glacier in darkness.
descent_text: The traverse climbs the north faces of the four Gunsight summits and rappels their south sides. From South Peak, a rappel descent leads to the Blue Glacier; the last rappel is free-hanging over a gaping moat onto the glacier, so look for the line that clears it. Check every rappel anchor on the granite thoroughly before trusting it. Parties often finish this descent in darkness. The rappels land on the east side of the range: a party camped below the Blue Glacier walks down to camp, while one based at the Dome-Chickamin col must work south below the peaks, cross the Blizzard-Gunsight col back onto the Chickamin Glacier, and recross the glacier to the col. Allow 3-4 hours, depending on snow and crevasse conditions on the glacier.
descent: Rappel the south side of each summit during the traverse; from South Peak, rappel to the Blue Glacier, finishing with a free-hanging rappel over the moat.
rappels: Rappel the south side of each summit as you traverse, then a rappel descent from South Peak to the Blue Glacier that ends in a free-hanging rappel over the moat. No count of rappels or stations is published.
rappel_count_note: The first-ascent party describes climbing the north faces of the four summits and rappelling their south sides, then rappelling from South Peak to the Blue Glacier, but gives no count or rope length for any of it. Expect to find or build your own anchors on the granite, and check every one.

pitch_detail.notes: Steep splitter granite hand crack; good protection; warm-up pitch on northeast face of Northeast Peak
Twin hand cracks and right-facing flake; excellent protection; sustained climbing
Face climbing on northeast face of Northeast Peak
Traverse to North Peak via solid granite with good protection on north face
Crack climbing on North Peak north face
Dead-end fist crack near North Peak summit; requires one point of aid (A1) to escape; pendulum move necessary
Traverse from North to Middle Peak notch; three pitches of moderate climbing in the notch (only section previously climbed)
Middle Gunsight north face; sustained crack climbing with excellent protection; four pitches of quality granite
Traverse to South Peak via mixed climbing and scrambling; three pitches of varied climbing
South Peak summit approach; short final pitch to highest point of South Gunsight
